clarification: k=floor(t·f_s), t_q=k/f_s; h(k,seed,channel)∈[0,1) debe ser un hash pseudoaleatorio determinista y sin estado.
ε_k=A(2h−1) produce jitter uniforme en [−A,A); usar amplitudes distintas y unidades explícitas para posición y ángulo.
assumptions: La misma semilla, índice y canal producen el mismo offset; no usar Math.random() por frame.

existing_equation_review.source_note: Regla procedural/artística; no se encontró una fuente primaria que prescriba exactamente esta combinación de cuantización y hash. No atribuirla a una publicación.

notes: u and frame/seed/channel are dimensionless integers; epsilon inherits the selected amplitude unit. Position and rotation amplitudes must never be conflated.

steps: Convert absolute time to an integer frame index k=floor(t*f_s), with f_s>0.
Mix frame, seed and channel through a fixed uint32 hash sequence; all arithmetic wraps modulo 2^32.
Map unsigned integer x to u=x/2^32, so u lies in [0,1).
Map u to a centered interval using epsilon=A*(2u-1), yielding [-A,A).
Use separate channel IDs and amplitudes for each position axis and each angular axis; hold the result constant for the entire sampled frame.

assumptions: The hash algorithm and constants are frozen as part of the project API; changing them changes every generated sequence.
All render evaluations use absolute time and the same seed/channel mapping.
Position and angle channels use distinct amplitudes with explicit units.
The hash is deterministic, not a cryptographic random generator and no statistical quality claim is made.
valid_domain: Finite t; f_s>0; integer seed/frame/channel; finite amplitude A>=0; uint32 hash arithmetic.
boundary_conditions: u=0 maps to -A; u approaches 1 but never equals 1, so the upper bound A is excluded.
A=0 produces zero jitter.
Negative time uses floor semantics for frame indexing.
Repeated (frame,seed,channel) must return exactly the same jitter.
inputs: Absolute time t and pose sample frequency f_s
Amplitude in a declared physical/scene unit
outputs: Deterministic bounded scalar offset for the selected channel
algorithm_steps: Validate finite time/frequency/amplitude and f_s>0, A>=0.
Compute integer frame with floor(t*f_s).
Mix frame, seed and channel using fixed uint32 hash constants and shifts.
Normalize unsigned hash to u in [0,1).
Return A*(2u-1); cache or recompute deterministically per frame.
technical_completion.pseudocode:
function jitter(t, fs, seed, channel, A):
  require finite(t,fs,A) and fs>0 and A>=0
  frame = floor(t*fs)
  x = uint32(frame*C1 + seed*C2 + channel*C3)
  x = avalanche32(x)  // fixed shifts and multipliers, modulo 2^32
  u = x / 4294967296
  return A*(2*u-1)

complexity.space: O(1) per channel; optional O(number of sampled frames) cache

threejs_binding.details: Evaluate from absolute animation time in the CPU rig update or a deterministic shader function. Use independent channels for x/y/z translation and rotation; keep jitter stable during the frame. The precise hash constants and uint32 semantics must match the tested reference.

steps: The distance constraint requires the new point q to lie on the line through anchor a and old point p, with ||q-a||=d.
Set u=(p-a)/||p-a||; then q=a+d*u. Since k=d/||p-a||, q=(1-k)a+k*p, which is dimensionally consistent because k is dimensionless.
Backward sweep fixes the end effector at t and projects each predecessor at its link length; forward sweep restores the root to its fixed base and projects each successor.
If target distance is at least total chain length, all links align along the root-to-target direction; this is the unreachable branch.

boundary_conditions: Unreachable if root-target distance >= sum(d_i); exact equality is fully extended.

steps: A rigid transform is encoded by a unit rotation quaternion q_r and a dual component q_d=0.5*(0,t)*q_r under the Hamilton product convention used by the implementation.

records.original_pseudocode: predict(); lambda=0; repeat iterations: for c: dl=solveConstraint(c,alpha/dt²,lambda); applyPositionCorrection(dl); velocity=(x-xPrev)/dt

clarification: La fórmula es la actualización incremental por restricción en un subpaso; Δλ se acumula en λ y Δx_i=w_i∇_iC·Δλ.
Reiniciar λ al comienzo de cada subpaso salvo que el solver documente otra estrategia; usar la misma convención de signo para C y gradientes.
assumptions: w_i son masas inversas; α es compliance según unidades de C; gradients y λ deben compartir formulación.
Definir subpasos, iteraciones, dt fijo y tratamiento de constraints degeneradas.
units: α_tilde=α/dt²; sus unidades dependen de C y de la escala de masa elegida.

notes: Para C con dimensión de longitud: ∇C es adimensional, w_i tiene kg^-1 y Σw_i||∇_iC||² tiene kg^-1.
La compliance α de la energía U=1/2 C²/α tiene s²/kg; α̃=α/Δt² tiene kg^-1, compatible con el denominador de Ec. (18).
El multiplicador λ tiene kg·m; α̃λ tiene m, compatible con C; Δx_i=w_i∇_iCΔλ tiene m.
Estas unidades cambian si C no es una distancia: α debe tener [C]²/[energía] y λ debe tener [masa]·[longitud]·[C]/[longitud] según la dimensión de ∇C; no reutilizar las unidades de distancia.

steps: Partir de la restricción escalar C(x)=0 y de la discretización implícita regularizada del artículo, Ecs. (8)-(9).
Aplicar la aproximación cuasi-Newton K≈M y asumir g(x_i,lambda_i)=0, explícitamente declaradas en §4, para obtener el sistema reducido (16).
Resolver el incremento del multiplicador mediante el paso Gauss-Seidel por restricción, Ec. (18): Δλ_j=−(C_j(x_i)+α̃_j λ_ij)/(∇C_j M⁻¹ ∇C_jᵀ+α̃_j).
Obtener la corrección posicional con Ec. (17): Δx=M⁻¹∇CᵀΔλ; acumular λ←λ+Δλ y x←x+Δx.
La escala de compliance es α̃=α/Δt² (definición en §4, anterior a Ec. (8)); no confundir la variante amortiguada de Ec. (26) con el núcleo elástico de Ec. (18).

assumptions: M es diagonal de masas positivas; M⁻¹ contiene masas inversas.
C_j es diferenciable en la configuración evaluada y el gradiente se calcula con la misma convención de signo que la corrección Δx.
Se usa el solver Gauss-Seidel y la aproximación K≈M de §4; no es el Newton exacto del sistema implícito.
α_j≥0 y Δt>0; λ_ij es el multiplicador total acumulado de esa restricción durante el subpaso.
La dimensión de α depende de la dimensión elegida para C; no existe una unidad única para todas las clases de restricciones.

Initialize solve positions x_0=x_tilde and one total multiplier λ_j=0 per constraint.
For each solver iteration, visit constraints in the declared Gauss-Seidel order.

Compute Δλ_j with Eq. (18); reject a singular zero denominator.

technical_completion.pseudocode:
xPred = x + dt*v + dt*dt*inverseMass * externalForce
xSolve = copy(xPred)
lambda = zeros(numberOfConstraints)
for iteration in 0 .. solverIterations-1:
    for constraint j in declaredGaussSeidelOrder:
        C = evaluateConstraint(j, xSolve)
        grad = evaluateGradient(j, xSolve)
        alphaTilde = compliance[j] / (dt*dt)
        denom = dot(grad, inverseMass * grad) + alphaTilde
        if not finite(denom) or denom <= 0:
            reportDegenerateConstraint(j); continue
        deltaLambda = -(C + alphaTilde*lambda[j]) / denom
        deltaX = inverseMass * grad * deltaLambda
        xSolve += deltaX
        lambda[j] += deltaLambda
xNext = xSolve
vNext = (xNext - xPrevious) / dt

Dividir el flujo saliente por el área proyectada de fibra a_o⊥=2 cosθ_o ds (Ec. (10)); usar el jacobiano de medio ángulo y comparar con Ec. (2) produce la BCSDF exacta de reflexión en Ec. (12): S_R=R/(8 cosθ_o cosθ_i) ∫D(ω_h1,ω_m1)G_{ω_m1}(ω_i,ω_o)dφ_m1.
Para GGX, la distribución de Appendix A Ec. (41) es D=β²/[π(1+(β²−1)(ω_h·ω_{mα})²)²]; Ec. (42) da ω_h·ω_{mα}=cosθ_h cosα cos(φ_h−φ_m)+sinθ_h sinα.

steps: El tensor de estructura suavizado define orientación φ y anisotropía A a partir de sus autovalores (Ecs. de §3.1).
La matriz S(A,α) y la rotación Rφ transforman el soporte circular en una elipse alineada con la estructura local (§3.2, definición de Ω).
Dividir el disco transformado en N sectores χ_i y suavizar sus máscaras: K_i=(χ_i*G_{σs})·G_{σr} (Ec. (1)); llevarlas a la elipse con w_i=K_i∘S R_{−φ} (Ec. (2)).
Calcular media ponderada m_i=(1/k)∫f(x)w_i(x−x₀)dx y varianza por canal s_i²=(1/k)∫f²(x)w_i(x−x₀)dx−m_i² (Ecs. (3)-(4)), con k=∫w_i.
Calcular α_i=1/(1+||s_i||^q) y salida Σ_i α_i m_i / Σ_i α_i; el artículo usa q=8 en sus ejemplos.
La aproximación discreta usa sumas y lookup bilineal de las máscaras; la normalización y el dominio de color deben coincidir con la definición de los pesos.
La fuente §3.2, p. 1960, declara que f usa valores enteros RGB (ej. 0..255), por lo que q=8 está calibrado para esa escala; no sustituir por RGB normalizado [0,1] sin cambiar la definición de pesos.

assumptions: La entrada es una imagen RGB f:R²→R³; la publicación realiza sus cálculos en RGB.

La norma ||s_i|| y la escala de valores de color deben ser coherentes con la publicación; el peso no es 1/(1+varianza) ni 1/(1+varianza escalar) salvo que se defina explícitamente una variante.

Pull sector weights back to the local anisotropic ellipse

equations.derivation_ref: Kyprianidis et al. 2009 §3.2 immediately after Eq. (4)

algorithm_steps: Compute RGB derivatives using Gaussian derivative kernels Gσ,x and Gσ,y.
Construct the 2×2 structure tensor (E,F;F,G) and smooth each tensor component.
Compute eigenvalues λ1, λ2, the minimum-gradient eigenvector t, orientation φ=arg(t), and anisotropy A=(λ1−λ2)/(λ1+λ2).
Build S=diag(α/(α+A),(α+A)/α), rotate the support by φ, and define the elliptical domain Ω.
For each sector i, evaluate K_i using Eq. (1) and pull it back to Ω using Eq. (2).
For each sector, compute weighted RGB mean m_i and variance s_i² using Eqs. (3)-(4), with k=∫w_i.
Compute α_i=1/(1+||s_i||^q) in the source's integer RGB code-value scale; output the normalized weighted mean.
Apply an explicitly selected image-edge sampling mode; this is an implementation contract, not fixed by the continuous equations.
technical_completion.pseudocode:
for each output pixel x0:
    fx, fy = gaussianDerivativeConvolutions(rgbImage)
    J = smoothStructureTensor(fx*fx, fx*fy, fy*fy)
    lambda1, lambda2, t = eigenSystem(J)
    phi = atan2(t.y, t.x)
    A = (lambda1-lambda2)/(lambda1+lambda2) if lambda1+lambda2>0 else 0
    S = diag(alpha/(alpha+A), (alpha+A)/alpha)
    for sector i in 0 .. N-1:
        wi = pullbackSectorKernel(i, S, phi, sigmaS, sigmaR)
        k = sum(wi)
        if k <= 0: mark sector invalid; continue
        mean[i] = sum(rgb*wi)/k
        variance[i] = max(sum(rgb*rgb*wi)/k - mean[i]*mean[i], 0)
        stddevNorm[i] = norm(sqrt(variance[i]))
        weight[i] = 1/(1 + stddevNorm[i]^q)
    output[x0] = sum(weight[i]*mean[i])/sum(weight[i])

steps: Reynolds §3, pp. 28-29, define tres solicitudes conductuales por prioridad: collision avoidance, velocity matching y flock centering; no define la suma ws*S+wa*(A−v)+wc*(C−p) del manifiesto.
Cada comportamiento produce una solicitud de aceleración 3D con magnitud truncada a 1 o menos por convención del sistema; una fuerza s_b∈[0,1] atenúa esa solicitud.

La implementación original actual usa prioritized acceleration allocation: acumular solicitudes en orden de prioridad, sumar sus magnitudes y detenerse al agotar a_max; recortar la última solicitud para que la magnitud total asignada no exceda a_max.

La suma ponderada del manifiesto se conserva como variante propia sólo si S, A−v y C−p se convierten primero a aceleración con parámetros de unidades compatibles. No presentarla como ecuación de Reynolds.
Integración explícita semimplícita: v_{n+1}=v_n+a_nΔt; p_{n+1}=p_n+v_{n+1}Δt. Es una elección de implementación documentada, no fórmula única del paper.

assumptions: Los comportamientos se calculan desde percepción local; Reynolds define una zona de sensibilidad esférica y menciona ponderación inversa exponencial de distancia.
Cada request es vector de aceleración y está truncado a magnitud ≤1 antes de aplicar strength.
Las solicitudes se entregan en orden explícito de prioridad; el orden no debe depender del orden accidental de iteración de un array sin documentar.
La integración y los límites de velocidad son extensiones del proyecto y deben declarar sus parámetros.

boundary_conditions: a_max=0 o strength=0 produce aceleración asignada cero.
Si una solicitud tiene norma cero, se ignora sin normalizar.
Si la suma de magnitudes no supera a_max, se conservan las solicitudes completas.

algorithm_steps: Compute local neighbors using an explicitly declared radius and perception/sensitivity policy.
Generate separate acceleration requests for collision avoidance, velocity matching and flock centering.
Clamp each behavior request to unit magnitude or less and multiply by its strength in [0,1].
Process requests in strict priority order, accumulating vector acceleration and accumulated request magnitudes.
If a request exceeds the remaining acceleration budget, scale that request to the remaining magnitude and stop.
Integrate velocity and position with the selected time integrator; this integrator is an implementation convention.
technical_completion.pseudocode:
acceleration = [0,0,0]
usedMagnitude = 0
for request in requests ordered by priority:
    require finite3(request.vector) and 0 <= request.strength <= 1
    v = clampMagnitude(request.vector, 1) * request.strength
    magnitude = length(v)
    remaining = maxAcceleration - usedMagnitude
    if remaining <= 0: break
    if magnitude > remaining:
        v = v * (remaining / magnitude)
        magnitude = remaining
    acceleration += v
    usedMagnitude += magnitude
    if usedMagnitude >= maxAcceleration: break
velocityNext = velocity + acceleration * dt
positionNext = position + velocityNext * dt

steps: Beer-Lambert attenuation solves dT/ds=-mu_t(s)T with T(0)=1; separation gives dT/T=-mu_t ds.
Integrating yields ln T(s)=-integral mu_t ds, hence T(s)=exp(-integral mu_t ds).
For constant mu_t over a segment of length Delta s, the segment transmittance is exp(-mu_t Delta s), so alpha=1-exp(-mu_t Delta s).
Front-to-back compositing adds the segment's conditional source radiance weighted by the incoming transmittance and segment opacity; the remaining transmittance multiplies by 1-alpha.
rho in the current kernel is a dimensionless density multiplier. If physical mass density is used instead, sigma_t must be a mass-specific coefficient and units must be changed consistently.

assumptions: Single-scattering/locally constant source approximation; not a complete solution of the radiative transfer equation.
Source S_i is defined as the radiance contribution conditioned on an extinction event in segment i; it is not an arbitrary per-unit-length source term.
Segment density and source are treated as constant within each step.
Radiance is accumulated in linear light and the opaque background is composed as L_total=L_acc+T_final*L_background.
valid_domain: sigma_t>=0 m^-1; rho>=0 dimensionless; Delta s>=0 m; finite source radiance; ray samples ordered front to back.
boundary_conditions: sigma_t=0 or rho=0 or Delta s=0 gives alpha=0 and unchanged transmittance.
For a homogeneous medium total transmittance is independent of subdivision up to floating-point error.
Very large mu_t*Delta s makes alpha approach 1; use numerically stable expm1 when required.
Negative extinction or segment length is invalid.

steps: Schlick's Eq. (15) defines a function with endpoint conditions F(0)=1, F(1)=F0, F'(1)=0 and F''(1)=0.
Set the polynomial as F(u)=F0+(1-F0)g(u), with g(1)=g'(1)=g''(1)=0 and g(0)=1.
The lowest-degree polynomial satisfying those constraints is g(u)=(1-u)^3 times a quadratic; imposing the derivative constraints yields the fifth power used in Eq. (15).
All terms are dimensionless; the power is a scalar approximation, not the complete Fresnel equations or a complete BRDF.

F0 is scalar for an ideal dielectric and may be RGB for a conductor/material parameterization.
u must represent the cosine argument of the selected BRDF convention; for a common Cook-Torrance shader this is V·H, not automatically N·V.
The equation assumes grazing reflectance 1.0; Schlick's more general F90 form is a distinct extension.
